analysis_options.entrypoint: production Action entry points on one Funcdata per case: Ghidra fd.getMerge().{mergeAddrTied,groupPartials,mergeMarker,mergeOpcode(CPUI_COPY),mergeAdjacent} on the persistent Funcdata member; Rust coreaction.rs-style fresh Merge::new() per Action calling merge_addr_tied/group_partials/merge_marker, merge_opcode, merge_adjacent, with the cross-Action channels round-tripping through Funcdata::merge_state
analysis_options.premise: covers are allocated at setHighLevel exactly as Funcdata::assignHigh does (funcdata_varnode.cc:52-53) and rebuilt lazily by HighIntersectTest::updateHigh during the Actions; the fixture never pre-installs covers
analysis_options.normalization: none; stdout is byte-diffed and both stderr streams must be empty

cases: case copy_shadow_ladder: blocks b0->b1; b0: op1 reg:0x10 vnP = COPY const 0x11
b1: op2 reg:0x20 vnQ1 = COPY vnP; op3 reg:0x30 vnQ2 = COPY vnP; op4 reg:0x40 tA = INT_ADD vnP,1; op5 reg:0x50 tB = INT_ADD vnQ2,2; op6 reg:0x60 tC = INT_ADD vnQ1,3
case disjoint_copy: single block b0; op1 reg:0x10 vnX = COPY const 0x21; op2 reg:0x20 vnY = COPY vnX

case pipeline_tail: same ladder graph at base 0x7200; the four staged Actions plus ActionMergeType — Ghidra mergeByDatatype(beginLoc,endLoc) (coreaction.hh:414-415), Rust Merge::merge_all (the production coreaction.rs ActionMergeType entry) — closing the nested-attach blind spot

Action sequence per case: setHighLevel (coreaction.hh:346); mergerequired = mergeAddrTied + groupPartials + mergeMarker (coreaction.hh:369-370, coreaction.cc:5718); mergecopy = mergeOpcode(CPUI_COPY) (:5722); mergeadjacent = mergeAdjacent (:5726)

Ghidra side drives all stages through the one persistent fd.getMerge() object; Rust side constructs Merge::new() per Action exactly like coreaction.rs applies, so persistence must round-trip through Funcdata::merge_state

per-stage observation: HighVariable instance counts of the six named varnodes, all fifteen pairwise shared-High identity booleans, and each named Varnode's rebuilt Cover as [block:uindex-uindex,...] with b/e endpoint encoding

case type_gate: single block; input reg:0x08(8B); op1 reg:0x10 SH=COPY const; op2 reg:0x18 F=COPY const; op3 reg:0x30 TSH=INT_LEFT(big, SH) 4B; op4 reg:0x38 TF=FLOAT_TRUNC(F) 4B — pins shift slot1 nochar equality (size 4) and FLOAT_TRUNC (INT,FLOAT) meta rejection

case float_trunc_cast: single block at 0x7400; op1 reg:0x10 SHX=COPY const 0x51; op2 reg:0x18 F2=COPY const 0x52; op3 reg:0x30 TF=FLOAT_TRUNC(F2) 4B same-size cast shape; op4 reg:0x38 C=COPY(SHX) control — the (Int,Float) ctor pair (typeop.cc:1913) keeps TF unmerged at mergeadjacent while the COPY control merges at mergecopy

case char_gate_null (0x7500) / char_gate_char (0x7600): single block; input reg:0x08(8B); op1 reg:0x10(1B) SH1=COPY const; op2 reg:0x20(4B) SH4=COPY const; op3 reg:0x30(1B) T1=INT_LEFT(big,SH1); op4 reg:0x38(4B) T4=INT_LEFT(big,SH4) — the SAME graph run under two core-type registrations

char_gate_null world: fixture registers only xunknown* (type_nochar null, type.cc:3131), so getBaseNoChar(1,TYPE_INT) IS getBase(1,TYPE_INT) (type.cc:3624) and the 1-byte shift pair T1/SH1 passes the merge.cc:1001 gate and merges like the size-4 control T4/SH4

char_gate_char world: a second FixtureArchitecture registers custom-named signed_byte_custom(non-ASCII INT1) and ascii_glyph_custom(ASCII INT1), then caches. type_nochar and typecache[1][INT] are different canonical objects independent of spelling, so T1/SH1 is rejected while T4/SH4 merges; Rust clears a TypeFactory, registers the same properties/names, caches, mounts it via fd.set_arch, and compares get_base/get_base_no_char Arcs
